newsitem.title: USA: Judge sides with Los Angeles agency in Lazard case.
newsitem.headline: Judge sides with Los Angeles agency in Lazard case.

text.p: A judge has rejected Lazard Freres & Co's motion to dismiss a Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority municipal bond suit, attorneys said on Monday.
The Superior Court judge's decision will allow the suit to move forward, said Robert Palmer, the authority's attorney.
In April, the Los Angeles authority sued Lazard Freres, joining a suit by former investment banker Michael Lissack.
The lawsuit, which seeks at least $14 million, was filed in California Superior Court under the California False Claims Act, a law providing financial incentives to whistleblowers.
Lazard Freres, which dropped out of the municipal industry in December but maintains a financial advisory unit, has denied any wrongdoing.
The lawsuit alleged Lazard Freres overcharged the Los Angeles authority by more than $3 million on a purchase of $542 million of Treasuries used in a 1993 bond deal.
The county had paid Lazard Freres $1.8 million over three years to serve as its financial adviser on bond deals, including the 1993 refunding.
Under the False Claims Act, the county can recover three times the damages, which includes the $3 million alleged overcharge and the $1.8 million advisory fee, the suit said.
The suit also alleged that Lazard Freres breached its fiduciary duty, breached its contract and violated sections of the state civil and government codes.
The suit, though filed in Los Angeles, has been transferred to San Francisco.
